purpose: Propose a reporting hierarchy over discovery mechanisms; retain every leaf definition and candidate decision for adjudication. Parent membership is not an assertion that mechanisms or issues are equivalent.
rules: Use training definitions/evidence only; held-out bytes may be checked for integrity but must not inform taxonomy or eligibility proposals.
Exactly one proposed primary parent per discovery leaf, with original leaf retained; never overwrite ledger labels or canonical records.
Security and correctness parents remain separate. Correctness origin still requires an explicit non-security screen; security linkage still requires a demonstrated trust boundary.
Choose the most specific evidenced leaf before using broad incomplete-case/state/context labels; unresolved overlaps require explicit review, not automatic relabelling.
Classify the causal mechanism rather than the consequence or changed syntax. A defect causing an exception can still be a representation, grammar or context defect.
Parent grouping is a training-derived proposal, not a fixed final category count or a response to support thresholds. Preserve distinct leaf interfaces and assumptions.
Eligibility, bounded-context sufficiency, paired-negative validity and independence remain separate pending decisions for every candidate, including assistant-supported cases.
Count family/repository unions within a parent directly; do not sum child-family counts. Mechanical families and dependence components are not independently adjudicated issues.
Zero supported discovery cases do not mean impossible mechanisms or zero held-out prevalence; retain tentative leaves for training-evidence resolution before freeze.
Cues in generated work queues are literal-text retrieval aids with exact source fields, not automatic eligibility or observability decisions.

parents.name: Text, bytes and serialization representation contracts
parents.include: Established operations lose required value representation across codec, bytes/text, scalar serialization, capacity, whitespace or record/newline boundaries.
parents.exclude: Type admission before a conversion, structural dtype/axis identity, presentation-only changes without a functional contract, and security interpretation boundaries.
parents.boundary_rule: Retain direction: XML requires textual scalar leaves whereas native Python export preserves scalars. Trimming required URL-attribute whitespace is normalization, not meaningful literal-space loss. Newline/style eligibility remains unresolved.

parents.name: Structural, dtype and semantic metadata identity
parents.include: A supported transformation loses, mismatches or incorrectly retains an established dtype, constructor, coordinate, label, shape or semantic metadata invariant.
parents.exclude: Arbitrary display preferences, intentionally changed representation, numerical algorithms with correct structural identity, and newly introduced subclass/type features.
parents.boundary_rule: Preservation and invalidation are opposite invariant obligations; never replace them with a generic always-preserve rule. Constructor class, dtype, metadata and value/label identity stay distinct leaves.

parents.name: Caller context, options and configuration precedence
parents.include: An existing operation receives substituted context, loses a supplied option, forces an omitted value or masks an established configuration override.
parents.exclude: New interfaces/features, diagnostic-only forwarding, intentional policy changes and security identity/binding defects.
parents.boundary_rule: Omitted downstream default, explicit option propagation and configuration-source precedence are not aliases. Inspect producer and consumer; a caller adapting to a new callee is not automatically a defective pair.

parents.name: Input admission and operation dispatch contracts
parents.include: A supported validation/dispatch contract admits an invalid structural or semantic form, bypasses required lookup checks or fails to select the operation for an established case.
parents.exclude: Newly supported cases, text conversion after valid admission, intentional API/policy revisions and security authorization/filtering without a separate boundary analysis.
parents.boundary_rule: Use specific grammar, semantic-type, dimensionality, lookup or rule-applicability leaf when evidenced. Incomplete-case handling is a residual discovery bucket requiring case-by-case refinement, not a generic final diagnosis.

parents.name: Value normalization, parsing and resource/command composition
parents.include: Accepted structured values are split, normalized, joined or rewritten under the wrong grammar or consumer representation, losing their intended component identity.
parents.exclude: Lossy byte codecs, incorrect caller base context, security destination/command policy, and tolerant interpretations introduced as new features.
parents.boundary_rule: Distinguish raw delimiter parsing from command option positioning and from URL normalization/resolution. Metadata coercion requires an established accepted-type contract; normalization is not validation or authorization.

parents.name: Empty, short and endpoint collection contracts
parents.include: An admitted empty/short/boundary state violates a required access, reduction or endpoint-enumeration precondition.
parents.exclude: Forbidden empty/short inputs, unconditional exception suppression, numerical zero normalization and newly changed endpoint policy.
parents.boundary_rule: Retain absent-neighbor, empty sequence, missing tail, empty reduction and inclusive endpoint witnesses. A local guard need not repair other boundaries or the caller's unchanged iteration count.

parents.name: Numerical, measurement and selective-update invariants
parents.include: An established algorithm uses wrong zero-result semantics, incompatible units, unsorted reference data, entity-counting unit or target mask.
parents.exclude: Arbitrary numeric/output differences, warning-only changes, unsupported inputs and security cryptographic or resource bounds.
parents.boundary_rule: Keep each causal invariant: arithmetic zero may require infinity while zero-contribution normalization may require finite zero. Sorting must permute associated values; deduplication/counting and update-target masks are distinct.

parents.name: Expected recovery and state-transition integrity
parents.include: A supported recoverable condition aborts progress, recovery replays consumed data, or required transition operations are omitted/misordered.
parents.exclude: Unexpected failures that should propagate, diagnostics alone, unsupported recovery promises and security lifecycle/availability boundaries.
parents.boundary_rule: State-transition is broad and must retain explicit starting/target state and actual operations; ordering cannot be inferred from a diff alone. Buffer replay is not generic duplicate counting.

parents.name: Machine-consumed error classification and result protocols
parents.include: An established machine consumer receives the wrong error class/status or a malformed exception-result protocol.
parents.exclude: Cosmetic wording, warning/logging migrations without a functional contract and arbitrary changes between nonzero exits.
parents.boundary_rule: An operation already failing with a different status was not previously accepted. Error tuple ordering can prevent required error recording; logging visibility alone needs its own admitted contract.

parents.name: Authorization identity, resource and enforcement binding
parents.include: A principal, resource identifier or accepted policy representation loses the binding required by an actual authorization consumer.
parents.exclude: Authentication-factor checks, merely absent decorators, ordinary metadata casing and speculative authorization impact without a consumer.
parents.boundary_rule: Resource scope, redundant ID disagreement, subject races, case normalization and literal-to-policy-regex injection retain distinct prerequisites; shared consequence does not merge issues.

parents.name: Authentication, credential validity and session lifecycle
parents.include: Authentication identity/factor/algorithm, derived-token validity, required reauthentication, guessing controls or session invalidation fails under an established account policy.
parents.exclude: Resource authorization after valid authentication, permitted refresh policies, harmless equality and rate controls assumed absent without inspecting effective controls.
parents.boundary_rule: Do not turn MFA bypass into passwordless compromise, parent-expiry preservation into universal token revocation, or session-level logout into global throttling. Keep distinct lifecycle leaves.

parents.name: Browser request, origin and method policy
parents.include: Ambient-authority browser actions or credentialed responses lack required initiator/token, credential-source, origin or request-method restrictions.
parents.exclude: Read-only operations, equivalent effective protections and claims that restricting request method alone implements complete CSRF protection.
parents.boundary_rule: CORS response-reading permission, CSRF request binding, ambient-cookie source selection and submission-method gating are related browser boundaries, not interchangeable vulnerabilities.

parents.name: Sensitive-data exposure through operational outputs and storage
parents.include: Established sensitive values reach diagnostics, object/request paths, process arguments or readable log files beyond their intended audience, or required redaction misses equivalent fields.
parents.exclude: Nonsecret identifiers, hypothetical public visibility and claims that one sink redaction secures all logs/caches or existing file modes.
parents.boundary_rule: Trace secret producer, actual sink and reader permissions for each leaf. New redaction policy entries do not prove key-normalization failure; umask does not fix existing files.

parents.name: Network destination, redirect and outbound credential isolation
parents.include: A network request/redirect or automatically attached sensitive content crosses its intended destination boundary because destination selection, routing control or credential removal is insufficient.
parents.exclude: Ordinary URL joining, trusted destinations, redirects without sensitive forwarding and universal SSRF claims from one host/IP check.
parents.boundary_rule: Open redirect, server-side destination/IP checks, internal proxy-option injection, initial credential scope and redirect body/header disclosure remain distinct. Scheme-host-port origin and domain/subdomain policy are not equivalent.

parents.name: Transport peer verification and truthful assurance state
parents.include: A required TLS peer verification is absent or an assurance indicator forgets an effective verification exception across its lifecycle.
parents.exclude: Encryption alone assumed authentication, cosmetic color changes and claims that correcting an indicator repairs certificate acceptance policy.
parents.boundary_rule: Actual verification and reporting of retained exceptions are separate obligations; preserve runtime defaults and exception-lifecycle context.

parents.name: Data crosses an executable language or option interpretation boundary
parents.include: Lower-trust values become Python/generated/template/shell/SQL syntax or executable program options instead of remaining data operands.
parents.exclude: Authorized source/option authorship, generic subprocess/regex use and escaping rules transferred across incompatible language contexts.
parents.boundary_rule: Retain sink-specific grammars. Argv separation does not stop option injection; HTML escaping is not template-source separation; generated source is not executed merely by being written.

parents.name: Trust and capability controls for loaded executable content
parents.include: Lower-trust templates, deserialized constructors/globals or automatically discovered executable configuration receive capabilities beyond their intended trust boundary.
parents.exclude: Trusted explicit configuration/template authorship, parsing without construction/evaluation and universal sandbox/allowlist safety claims.
parents.boundary_rule: Do not conflate data inserted into trusted source with deliberately supplied source lacking a sandbox. Template-sandbox leaf has only ambiguous training evidence at this checkpoint.

parents.name: Browser content interpretation, serving and embedding policy
parents.include: Untrusted rendered/served content or frame embedding crosses an established browser-facing interpretation policy.
parents.exclude: Assuming every HTML value executes, template evaluation, harmless file types and missing headers where equivalent effective policy exists.
parents.boundary_rule: HTML escaping, active data URI filtering, upload disposition/origin policy and anti-framing are distinct leaves requiring consuming browser/deployment evidence.

parents.name: Filesystem path, target and artifact trust boundaries
parents.include: Lower-trust inputs select files outside an intended root, become unintended local reads/writes or supply artifacts via predictable existing workspaces.
parents.exclude: Authorized arbitrary paths, secure atomic creation and claims of race-free confinement from separate pathname checks.
parents.boundary_rule: Read primitive, root escape, predictable symlink target and pre-existing workspace trust are distinct mechanisms; inspect actual sink and process identity for each.

parents.name: Input/resource limits, parser failures and concurrent lifecycle availability
parents.include: An established lower-trust availability boundary is affected by input size/work, costly parsing, unhandled admitted states, lock reentry or socket-close lifecycle races.
parents.exclude: Ordinary performance changes, trusted computation, one request failure presented as proven process-wide outage and universal safety claims from a local bound/guard.
parents.boundary_rule: Retain size, multiplicity, regex, entity expansion, decode/null failure, lock and socket leaves. Non-reentrant lock and descriptor lifetime are not generic parser DoS; no exact complexity or reproduction is inferred.

parents.name: Differential HTTP message framing
parents.include: Relevant HTTP frontend/backend parsers disagree on message boundaries after nonstandard length, coding, line or whitespace interpretation.
parents.exclude: Every syntax relaxation, standalone decoder correctness without a production boundary and universal smuggling safety claims.
parents.boundary_rule: Retained as a standalone parent rather than forced into availability or generic input validation; require concrete differential parsing and error/consumption behavior.

parents.name: Cryptographic derivation, unpredictability and observable verification
parents.include: A cryptographic protocol requires output length, unpredictable values or resistance to observable secret/padding distinctions that the inspected implementation fails to provide.
parents.exclude: Generic equality/randomness, public-data validation and claims masked Python source proves constant time or practical exploitation.
parents.boundary_rule: KDF length, nonce generation, ordinary secret comparison and RSA padding oracles have different assumptions and measurements; preserve each leaf and protocol consumer.

parents.name: Generated contract representation, validation and memory extents
parents.include: Compiler-emitted contract operations violate logical bytestring equality, external-return type bounds or copy/allocation memory extents across an evidenced contract security boundary.
parents.exclude: Python host memory unsafety inferred from code generation, enum-only refactors, equivalent helper changes and universal contract safety.
parents.boundary_rule: Keep equality, ABI validation and copy capacity separate. Adjudication concerns emitted IR/layout and consuming contract use; Python function text is not the executed contract.

parents.name: Whole-message content policy enforcement
parents.include: An unrelated permitted token short-circuits required moderation of independently prohibited content.
parents.exclude: Intended per-token exemption, ordinary regex matching and claims every deployment enables the filter.
parents.boundary_rule: Retain standalone policy semantics; do not fold moderation into resource authorization or HTML escaping merely to reduce category count.

parents.name: Operational log record integrity
parents.include: Lower-trust record delimiters forge or corrupt entries in an actual line-oriented log sink.
parents.exclude: Secret disclosure through intact records, every interpolated value and complete terminal/encoding safety claims.
parents.boundary_rule: Record integrity is separate from confidentiality and browser HTML interpretation; preserve sink-specific delimiter and formatter evidence.

priority_boundary_reviews.decision: Refine broad mechanisms using existing per-candidate training evidence; separate supported alternatives and actual state/context contracts from features and coordinated interfaces.
No current assistant-supported training cases. Resolve evidence/eligibility or retain explicit tentative/unresolved status; do not promote based on parent support.
Same parent, opposite interface direction. Retain leaf-specific expected result and never call the fixes equivalent.
Do not transfer complete CSRF protection, response-read access or mutation reachability between distinct browser-boundary mechanisms.
After-code constant-time properties remain unproven; preserve conditional negative scope and actual runtime/protocol observability.

curated_lineage_reviews.proposal: One conservative version-dependence review block; original upstream-operand repair and introduced short-tail regression remain distinct mechanism leaves. Independent issue split/merge pending.

curated_lineage_reviews.evidence: Exact earlier after/later before function hash and inspected paired reader migration followed by per-invocation environment-scope change.
curated_lineage_reviews.proposal: One conservative version-dependence review block with caller-component eligibility unresolved; preserve all shared-fix shell siblings. Independent issue split/merge pending.
